Purpose and exclusions

A defeated creature yields a server-created loot allocation with guaranteed entries and weighted rolls. The allocation is generated once per defeat/recipient policy; opening the corpse again never rerolls rarity or produces a second entitlement.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create URPGLootDefinition and DA_Loot_Mossfang with guaranteed cloth scrap plus one weighted pool. Use test weights CommonMaterial=90, RareToken=9, NoDrop=1 only as a fixture.
  2. Create BP_LootContainer with interaction interface and stable allocation reference. Enemy corpse can use it directly or spawn a view actor; choose one representation path per entry.
  3. Build WBP_Loot with entry selection, take-all, pending/rejected states and clear ownership text.
  4. Reopen FinalizeDefeat to create/trigger the allocation exactly once after eligible defeat commit; reopen inventory capacity service and owner snapshot observer.
  5. Place two clients at one corpse, one eligible and one unrelated, plus a full-bag fixture. Restore the same corpse from persisted state for reload testing.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Guaranteed/random loot, corpse access and replay safety. Rule owner: URPGLootComponent. This asset’s role is A defeated creature yields a server-created loot allocation with guaranteed entries and weighted rolls. The allocation is generated once per defeat/recipient policy; opening the corpse again never rerolls rarity or produces a second entitlement.

  1. Committed defeat ledger provides eligibility and loot-table version. Validate every item/family ID before enabling the encounter.
  2. Server/backend selects each guaranteed and weighted outcome once, recording resolved entries and random audit context without exposing secret seeds to clients.
  3. Replicate the existence/available state of the corpse and send only the eligible player their loot details. An optional visible pickup references the same allocation entry, not a second reward.
  4. Player chooses entries; server repeats range, ownership and current allocation checks and submits one claim command.
  5. Database transaction locks allocation and inventory, checks capacity, transfers exact entries/currency and marks them claimed with receipt/revision. NoSpace leaves unclaimed entries intact.
  6. UI displays committed inventory result and remaining allocation. Corpse reload/reconnect queries existing allocation, never invokes generation again.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Corpse_Mossfang_01 / Party_AB. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Unrelated character opens personal allocation -> NotEligible; no entry details leaked.
Claim replay -> original result/AlreadyClaimed, no extra item.
Full bag -> NoSpace with allocation unchanged; currency-only claims follow explicit separate entry selection.
Missing loot item definition -> encounter content validation fails or loot quarantined with MissingLootDefinition, never substitute an arbitrary reward.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.
